method: Phase 2: blind re-author all 12 sufficiency goldens + 5 profile goldens from scenario/requirement/view alone; then adversarial read of F8, deficiency order, relation registry, knownLimitations; suite check-fact-plane.py OK + 10/10 selftest

suiteState.check: OK — 12 sufficiency + 5 profile goldens, F1..F11 clean

sufficiency.note: First instinct considered a dedicated coverage-unknown code; D9 vocabulary has no fact-view coverage code; required-relation-missing under completeness=complete is the correct TO-5 face.
Rung is met; completeness demand fails for budget reason — discrimination order correctly prefers budget-exhausted over required-relation-missing.

independent.deficiency: UNMAPPED — confidence shortfall is not any of the four discrimination cases

sufficiency.note: See finding R1-FP-01. Independent author would not pick required-relation-missing (remedy 'widen scope' is wrong).
Propagating the dependency's rungUnavailableBecause is right; if calls were language-tier, language-tier-unsupported should win.

F8.question: Is F8 right — top rung of a one-rung ladder satisfied outright, no deficiency?
F8.answer: YES. This is the mechanical form of C-1. declares@syntactic is authoritative, not a degraded semantic. Without F8, C-1 is a slogan. Blind golden syntax-relation-is-authoritative confirms.
F8.ifF8Wrong: C-1 would not be implementable as stated — I do not find F8 wrong.

fourWayDeficiency.question: Is four-way deficiency discrimination right, and is most-specific-remedy precedence correct?
fourWayDeficiency.answer: The four codes (language-tier, provider, budget, relation-missing) are the right REMEDY classes for rung/coverage failures. Precedence by remedy specificity is a judgment, not measured — acceptable if documented. Gap: confidence-floor is outside the four cases (R1-FP-01). Simultaneous causes still collapse to one code; secondary causes are D9's secondaryDeficiencies, not fact-plane's — acceptable cross-surface split if stated.
fourWayDeficiency.residual: A view that is both provider-unavailable and budget-exhausted reports only the more-specific code; user may not get the faster-to-act-on cause.

relationRegistrySet.question: Is the relation registry the right SET?
relationRegistrySet.answer: SHAPE is the contract; membership is illustrative and honestly limited. Twelve relations cover inventory/syntax/semantic/derived enough to exercise ladders, dependencies, and one-rung C-1 cases. Not exhaustive — knownLimitation is correct. Do not seal membership as product inventory.

findings.title: Confidence-floor failure maps to required-relation-missing with the wrong remedy
findings.evidence: Golden confidence-floor-unmet: types@annotated present with confidence 0.4, minConfidence 0.9. Discrimination cases cover only language-tier / provider / budget / relation-absent. Checker falls through to required-relation-missing (check-fact-plane.py confidence branch). Remedy for that code is 'widen scope' — wrong for a confidence shortfall. D9 deficiency enum also lacks a confidence code, so F9 would block a freestanding fact-plane-only code unless D9 is extended or confidence is redefined as non-deficiency unsatisfied with a distinct field.
findings.impact: Callers and operators get a false remedy class. TO-7 says a code is a remedy class — this violates that intent for the confidence floor, which the requirement schema advertises.
findings.requiredChange: Either (a) add a D9+fact-plane deficiency for confidence shortfall with remedy 'improve producer / lower floor', or (b) remove minConfidence from the requirement schema until a remedy code exists, or (c) document that confidence shortfall is intentionally alias of required-relation-missing and change the published remedy text for that code to cover both — (a) preferred.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Evidence that confidence is never a caller-facing deficiency (e.g. producers always emit 1.0 or omit confidence) making the golden only a schema toy.

findings.title: Sufficiency goldens and sufficiency function still share one author for the 11 matching cases
findings.evidence: This review is a second author for the expected verdicts. 11/12 match and 1 real gap found. Residual co-authorship risk is reduced but not zero until another independent re-author (Reviewer 2 is not assigned this surface).
findings.impact: Same trap class as D9 v1.5 if only one independent re-author ever runs.
findings.requiredChange: Keep second-author re-author on file as seal evidence; optional third sample on any future golden additions.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: Automated property-based generation of goldens from the discrimination table with no human expected fields.

findings.title: Subject-set honesty for completeness=complete is still owned by REOPENED evidence surface
findings.evidence: knownLimitations correctly state F5 constrains the verdict but nothing proves coverage values are honest until retention/evidence subject-set commitment seals.
findings.impact: F5 can be gamed by a lying coverage flag. Architecture-complete for the fact-plane face; not product-complete for non-membership claims.
findings.requiredChange: Cross-link seal of FACT-PLANE to EVIDENCE subject-set commitment; do not publish universal-negative claims until that lands.
findings.whatWouldChangeMyMind: EVIDENCE surface sealed with measured subject-set commitment and F5 cross-check.

sealRecommendation.blocker: R1-FP-01 (confidence deficiency mapping). F8 and the other 11 goldens are sealable.
sealRecommendation.afterChanges: SEAL once confidence is a first-class remedy code or minConfidence is withdrawn from the public requirement schema.
